channel.title: Lochie's Research Briefings
channel.description: Private audio briefings generated from my research notes: Australian banks, insurance, and the Anthropic IPO.
channel.itunes:author: Lochie Halloway

item.title: Anthropic IPO 3: The Morningstar view against the price
item.description: A deeper look at Morningstar's US$1.7tn fair value: how Malik Ahmed Khan sizes the business, the growth drivers, what the bull and bear cases assume, the price range on both share counts, the economics of serving customers and the computing bill, the moat and where it is weakest, competition, control, the float and lock-ups, and the lines and numbers worth knowing. General information only, not advice.

item.title: Anthropic IPO: Mock interview practice
item.description: Twelve likely interview questions on the Anthropic float, with the agreed answers: the valuation, growth and losses, competition, the computing bill, partners that compete, safety, governance, how Australians can buy in, and whether it marks a turning point for AI. Two voices, host and Lochie. General information only, not advice.

item.title: Anthropic IPO 2: What Morningstar and PitchBook analysts think
item.description: Harrison Rolfes' five PitchBook notes and his $1.42tn fair value, the margin debate, compute commitments seen from Anthropic's and Broadcom's side, moats and commodification (Khan, Hawthorne), governance and index inclusion, and how to get exposure. General information only, not advice.

item.title: Anthropic IPO 1: The S-1 explained - how a frontier AI lab makes money
item.description: A walk through Anthropic's S-1/A (filed 2 Nov 2026): the training, serving and selling economics of a frontier lab, how each customer type is billed, the numbers, the $895bn compute commitments, peers, control, the offering and the IPO timeline. General information only, not advice.

item.title: CSL Behring: a plain-English tour of what it actually sells
item.description: The product portfolio explained without the share price or forecasts: plasma and immunoglobulin, haemophilia and gene therapy, emergency plasma products, hereditary angioedema and Andembry, and the one question to ask about any CSL product.
